# Djinni: human labels vs silver (generated by `python -m app.eval.djinni score`; do not edit)

Real anonymised CVs (Djinni, MIT), 8 JDs, 424 pooled pairs. Gold in use: **silver (mean of 2 LLM annotators; not human)**.
Quadratic-weighted Cohen's κ on the pairs both sides graded. Decision rule (EVAL.md §2): κ(human, silver) ≥ 0.8 keeps silver as the main set; ≥ 0.6 as a secondary set; below that the human labels replace it.

## Annotator quality check

Gold uses only annotators who pass: weighted κ ≥ 0.4 with at least one other annotator, and, for blind labels, a median of ≥ 10 s per pair (the page stamps every grade). Review-mode labels are fast by nature (accepting a shown grade) and count as anchored on the model.

| Annotator | mode | median s / pair | notes written | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| human Đán | blind | 1.4 | 0 | ❌ excluded: median 1.4 s per pair < 10 s |
| human Vũ | blind | 30.4 | 367 | ✅ usable |

Adjudicated human gold (v2.1) needs two annotators who pass the check; 1 do.
